key_insight: Flux oxygen content controls Marangoni flow direction and strength in submerged arc welding, shifting molten-pool behavior from wide spreading at low oxygen to deeper, narrower pools at high oxygen.
engineering_relevance: Tuning oxygen supply via flux composition offers a practical lever to control weld width, penetration depth, and solidification behavior in submerged arc welding.
method: Developed a coupled numerical framework for oxygen transport in the molten pool.
Included multi-pathway oxygen transport from the flux and dynamic, region-specific surface tension calculations.
Simulated molten-pool flow under varying oxygen contents to study convection reversal and pool-shape changes.
evidence_signal: Simulation results across multiple oxygen levels showed a transition from dominant outward spreading flow to stronger centripetal return flow, with higher oxygen producing an internal vortex, deeper penetration, and delayed rear solidification.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on numerical simulation, so experimental validation and careful calibration of oxygen transport and surface-tension parameters would be important before process transfer.
paper_title: Influence of Oxygen Content upon Molten Pool Dynamics in Submerged Arc Welding
